- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or too high after sharp price spikes in history.
- Model shows persistent lag in correcting downward trends; often underestimates sharp declines.
- Mean reversion is not adequately captured — forecasts stay too high longer than actual price reversion.
- Overshoot correction is delayed; model takes 2–3 days to adjust downward after a spike.
- Forecasts for 30-day horizon are overly optimistic, especially when recent history shows volatility or downward momentum.
- Model fails to account for sudden policy or market shocks — forecasts remain static despite sharp true price movements.
- When true price drops below 65, model often fails to adjust and continues to forecast above 68–70.
